chunks: And from him, from Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If his doubt is equal between three and four, he should give salām and pray two rakʿahs and four sajdahs with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb while seated, shortening the tashahhud.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Likewise, whoever becomes forgetful and does not know whether he is in the second or the fourth; if his presumption toward one of the two is stronger than the other, he acts according to his presumption. But if his presumption regarding them is equal, he builds upon being in the fourth, recites the tashahhud, and when he gives salām, he stands and prays two rakʿahs standing, reciting in each one of them al-Ḥamd alone; and if he wishes, he may recite tasbīḥ.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in the sitting portion of salat
key_terms.الثَّلَاثِ: the third rakʿah in the prayer count
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعِ: the fourth rakʿah in the prayer count
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah recited in the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs prayed as precautionary prayer
key_terms.سَوَاءً: equal, with neither side outweighing the other
key_terms.ظَنُّهُ: his stronger presumption or probable judgment
key_terms.وَهْمُهُ: his doubt or uncertainty regarding the number of rakʿahs

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat if they doubt whether they are in the third or fourth rakʿah, or the second or fourth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for doubt and forgetfulness in salat (prayer), especially when a person is uncertain between certain rakʿah counts. It explains when one should act on the stronger presumption and when one should complete the prayer on a particular basis and then perform precautionary rakʿahs afterward.
